question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{8{n}^{6}+4{n}^{5}}{8{n}^{4}+10}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
The dominant term in the denominator is $8{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8{n}^{6}+4{n}^{5}}{8{n}^{4}+10} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{8{n}^{6}}{{n}^{4}}+\frac{4{n}^{5}}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{8{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}+\frac{10}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8{n}^{2}+4n}{(8+\frac{10}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8{n}^{2}+4n}{8+0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }({n}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}n) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.
